append.row: | *Qui statis in domo Dómini, in átriis domus Dei nostri* (133:1b = 134:2) |
append.text: **Ps 134:2 departs: *Vós que estais de pé na casa do Senhor*** — after *louvai, servos, o Senhor* (and in the Tuesday Lauds antiphon, which sings 134:1a + 2a as one line) a bare *Que* hangs on *o Senhor*, making the Lord the one standing; *Vós que* names the addressees (DRB 'You that stand'; MS1932 *vós … que assistis*). Proposed for 133:1b too, so the twins match again; *Que estais* the option in 134. No v1/v2 reader objected.

**Ps 134:7b *ab hómine usque ad pecus* → *desde o homem até o gado*** (v2): the Latinist and the stylist both asked *gado* against v1's *animal* — pecus singular, livestock, beside *homem*; *animal* (MS1932 *até ao animal*) the option. *pécora* at 8:8 unaffected.

**Ps 134:7b *qui prodúcit ventos de thesáuris suis* → *Tira dos seus depósitos os ventos*** — the row followed; the stylist (v1) asked *tesouros* again ('depósitos' commercial) and the blind reader found *depósitos* odd for God's storehouses — held, *tesouros* the option. Now two psalms with the same objection.

**Ps 134:13 copies 101:13** (*Senhor, o vosso memorial, de geração em geração*). The stylist (v1) heard *memorial* as a monument or a legal brief and asked *memória*; the blind reader listed it unknown again — held for rule 6, *a vossa memória* the option.

**Ps 134:14 *et in servis suis deprecábitur* (the same Greek παρακληθήσεται) → *e para com os seus servos se deixará aplacar*** — 89:13's words, the Latin's order (verb last, after the stylist, who named v1 *se deixará aplacar para com os seus servos* his worst line). The Latinist (minor) asked *se deixará rogar*: refused, *deixar-se / fazer-se rogar* is heard in Brazil as reluctance; the stylist's *com os seus servos* refused (heard as the agent). *aplacar* unknown to the blind reader a second time.
**Ps 134:15 = 113:12** (*Os ídolos das nações são prata e ouro*); the Latinist asked *simulacros* again (minor), refused as there.

**Ps 134:7a *Edúcens nubes ab extrémo terræ* → *Faz sair as nuvens do extremo da terra*** (v2): v1 took the Greek's ἀνάγων (*Faz subir*, MS1932); the Latinist (minor) held it to the Latin verb — taken. The same verse has *prodúcit ventos*, given *Tira* (DM1962 *tira o vento dos cofres*) to keep the two verbs apart.

**Ps 134:7b *qui prodúcit ventos de thesáuris suis* (ἐξάγων) → *Tira … os ventos*** — the other sense, bring out (not make spring up); *fazer sair* taken by edúcere in the same verse; DM1962 *tira*. *Faz sair* the option (with *Faz subir* for 7a).

append.row: | cognóscere + *quóniam* (55:10 *ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es*) |
append.text: **Ps 134:5 *Quia ego cognóvi quod magnus est Dóminus* → *Porque eu sei que o Senhor é grande*** (v2): v1 *eu soube* (19:7a, 55:10) was heard as receiving news by both the stylist and the blind reader; here no *nunc* / *ecce* marks a moment, and the perfect of knowing states what is known (DRB 'I have known'). The CNBB LH has *Eu bem sei* (fetched). *soube*, *reconheci* (the stylist) and *conheci* are options. Proposed: *cognóvi* + clause without a time-word → *sei*.

**Ps 134:11 matches:** *Seon, rei dos amorreus, e Og, rei de Basã, * e todos os reinos de Canaã* (no *a*: the names are the Latin's nominatives in apposition to *reges fortes*, not objects; the CNBB LH *A Seon que foi rei amorreu* fetched, `ps134/circulation.md`).

**Ps 134:18 = 113:16** (*Façam-se semelhantes a eles aqueles que os fazem*): the stylist (v1) heard the *Façam-se … fazem* jingle and asked *Tornem-se … os que os fazem* — refused as at 113:16 (the echo is the Latin's *fiant / fáciunt*); *Tornem-se* the option.
